raw_response:
I farm only 4.5 mu, and my household is small, so I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on all of my land. That is the system I know best, it fits our well irrigation, and it is the safest way for me to keep grain production stable. Because some family labor is off-farm and I am already 68, I will not choose anything too complicated or too risky. I will use better seed, keep fertilizer at a moderate level, irrigate when the crop most needs water, and do only the pesticide sprays that are necessary. For wheat, I will focus on steady growth through winter and a good grain filling period in spring. For maize, I will focus on strong emergence after wheat harvest, enough fertilizer for summer growth, and moisture at key stages. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor and is practical for my small farm.
